quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Drivers from both directions can pass.
You can pass if you are at the top of a hill.
You can pass during daylight only.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic on the other side is moving toward you. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass, no matter which direction you are driving.

questions.question: When is street racing legal?
questions.explanation: Street racing is always illegal. High speeds make it impossible to react to road hazards. Street racing causes serious injuries and deaths.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right. Slow down to the speed shown.
A divided highway starts. Slow down to the speed shown.
Merge ahead. Slow down to the speed shown.
Winding road ahead. Slow down to the speed shown.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right. Slow down to the speed shown.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves to the right. You must slow down to the safe speed shown on the sign, which is 35 mph in this case.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: A lower speed zone is starting.
The lower speed zone has ended.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lower speed zone has ended.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit during the times shown. An "End school zone" sign marks where the lower speed zone ends.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a line through it mean on a sign?

options.text: Some drivers must yield to others.

questions.explanation: Signs with a red circle and slash are rectangular with red and black markings. A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is forbidden.

questions.question: When driving near large trucks, you must account for:

options.text: The longer distance they need to stop.
The shorter distance they need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer distance they need to stop.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay in places where the truck driver can see you. Do not block the truck driver's view of traffic.

questions.question: What happens to fines for traffic violations in work zones?
questions.explanation: In work zones with workers and warning signs present, all traffic fines are doubled.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols on yellow. This sign warns you of a steep hill ahead. Be ready to slow down for safety.

questions.question: You should not pass:

options.text: Where you cannot see clearly ahead.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on a hill, in a curve, or anywhere visibility is poor. Only pass where it is legal and safe.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up as fast as you can.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.explanation: A green light means you can go, but you must first let pedestrians and other traffic clear the intersection.

questions.question: When passing a stopped emergency vehicle, drivers should:

options.text: Move to a different lane or slow down.
Ask the emergency worker if they need help.
Move into the lane closest to the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane or slow down.
questions.explanation: You must move away from the lane closest to the emergency vehicle. If you cannot move safely, slow down instead.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead is now divided. Stay to the right of the divider.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates, you should:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
Make sure your vehicle can cross the tracks completely without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross the tracks completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Check that you have enough space to fully cross the tracks before entering. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Watches what other drivers are doing.
Drives at the same speed all the time.
Only drives in areas they know well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver watches other drivers and expects problems. This helps prevent accidents even when other drivers are distracted.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You may turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must come to a complete stop. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears, unless a sign says otherwise.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be in the area.

questions.question: In foggy weather, you should:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Never drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead. High beams reflect off fog and rain, making it harder to see.

questions.question: To stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Do not drive beside them and do not follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside them and do not follow too closely.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have big blind spots on the sides and back. Do not drive alongside them or tailgate them.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle:

options.text: On a curve or hill because oncoming traffic is unlikely.
By driving on the highway shoulder.
When your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Never pass on curves or hills—you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never pass by driving on the shoulder. Never pass across a solid yellow line.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen when you drink alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance gets worse.

questions.explanation: Alcohol slows reaction time, affects vision, distorts judgment, reduces recovery from glare, and often increases risky behavior. It does not improve focus.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You may only drive straight ahead.
You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.
Vehicles moving in any direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction the arrow points. Only go if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?

options.text: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system pushes harmful fumes out of your vehicle. A leak allows these fumes into the passenger area. Fix leaks right away to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams bounce off the fog and reflect back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Use fog lights if your vehicle has them.

questions.question: Why do you need to be extra careful when driving at night?

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: Darkness reduces your ability to see the road and other vehicles. You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or when objects are not visible from 500 feet away.

questions.question: What should you do when passing on a multilane highway?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before you pass, check that the passing lane is clear. Use your turn signal to show other drivers you are changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do if your wheels drop off the road onto the shoulder?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, reduce your speed without braking hard. Turn carefully back onto the road. Check for other traffic before returning to the road.

questions.question: What do diagonal stripes sloping downward to the left on a barricade mean?
questions.explanation: Diagonal stripes on a barricade show you which direction to go. Stripes sloping down to the right mean turn right. Stripes sloping down to the left mean turn left.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on top of water instead of gripping the road. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: When school bus lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Never pass on hills, curves, at intersections, at railroad crossings, on bridges, or in no passing zones. Do not pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side with a median or center turn lane.

questions.question: What do diagonal stripes sloping downward to the right on a barricade mean?
questions.explanation: Diagonal stripes on a barricade show you which direction to go. Stripes sloping down to the right mean turn right. Stripes sloping down to the left mean turn left.
